claims.text: The intervention is to add approximately 1–3 vol% high-quality, aligned graphene nanoplatelets to W–Cu and localize them at or near W/Cu interfaces.
Interfacial graphene nanoplatelets will increase the effective thermal conductivity of W–Cu.
Interfacial graphene nanoplatelets will allow W–Cu to retain mechanical durability.
Interfacial graphene nanoplatelets will allow W–Cu to retain irradiation resistance.
Graphene has exceptionally high in-plane thermal conductivity.
Graphene possesses high intrinsic mechanical strength and modulus.
Graphene at the W/Cu interface will act as a thermally conductive bridge.
Graphene at the W/Cu interface will reduce interfacial thermal resistance.
Aligned interfacial graphene will provide continuous and efficient heat-dissipation pathways through W–Cu.
Metal–graphene interfaces can impede or alter dislocation activity and strengthen metal–graphene composites.
Graphene is sufficiently chemically stable to maintain W/Cu interfacial integrity under mechanical stress and irradiation.
Maintaining interfacial integrity will prevent premature failure associated with thermal and radiation-induced defects.
The graphene-modified composite will have approximately 15–30% higher effective thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable graphene-free W–Cu composite.
The predicted thermal-conductivity improvement will occur without a significant loss of mechanical strength.
The predicted thermal-conductivity improvement will occur without a significant loss of irradiation tolerance.
The claimed benefit should hold under high heat flux, cyclic thermal loading, temperatures up to approximately 500 °C, and neutron or heavy-ion irradiation representative of fusion-reactor joints.
Excess graphene or graphene agglomeration may create weak spots or interfacial discontinuities and reduce composite coherence.
The benefit depends on irradiation dose and temperature remaining below levels that significantly degrade graphene.
He+ ion irradiation can be used as a surrogate to mimic relevant neutron-induced damage in the proposed comparison.
